decisions.reason: As a prominently announced new-generation core machine shown on the home page, it carries high development costs and strong public commitment, which makes management likely to persist with it.

Although a narrower software module is easier to withdraw than a machine, it was publicly launched as an extension of the firm's software portfolio and is likely to be retained as part of the installed-system offering.

This coder fits the firm's core industrial marking business, so despite only moderate visibility, sunk engineering effort and the tendency to blame weak uptake on temporary market factors support continuation.
The app is more peripheral and cheaper to discontinue than hardware, but as the named successor to an earlier app it reflects ongoing commitment and is still likely to be kept at least another year.

An inline code verification system is strategically complementary to coding equipment, and management is likely to maintain it to justify the broader traceability solution it has signaled to customers.
Because this software was visible on the home page and supports the use of the firm's printing systems, the firm has both reputational and ecosystem reasons to continue offering it.
